what: Ten kumquat-colored balls (three.js Phong material, radius 10 × 1~3) drift slowly in random directions from fixed spots on the panel at 5e-5 per ms (as a fraction of the panel half-width), and re-enter from the opposite side when they leave the panel (±1.05). A white light and an orange light shift with the mouse position so the balls’ bright side turns to follow the mouse. With look: fixed, the panel sticks to the screen and the balls are pushed up by the amount the page has scrolled (following with a .3 lag) — decorative balls floating inside photo boxes or between sections.

options.look: fixed — draws attached to the screen, not the panel (original default look). Default is inside the panel only
options.count: Ball count, default 10 (first ten of the original slots from the front)
options.speed: Flow speed (ratio of half the panel width per 1ms), default .00005 — 0 stops it
options.size: Ball radius (px), default 10 — 1 to 3 times per slot. Half below 840px
options.scroll: look: with fixed, the share that follows the scroll (per frame, at 60fps), default .3
options.--fx-ball · --fx-glow · --fx-shine: Ball color · lower-right light · upper-left light (via style), default --kf-accent-soft · --kf-accent · --kf-on-accent

use: — Load three.cjs first as window.THREE (see three-global.js)
note: The original turns one fixed full-screen canvas on and off per page (hide/show .5s · only the edge balls shrink by half) and on the first screen attaches the canvas to the document and clips it to the photo box shape (rect … round 24px) — the part generalizes this to one canvas attached per panel. With reduced motion, only one frame is drawn.

from.where: spheres.js (all pages — cut out and drawn inside the Hero photo box and the subpage header panel, and between sections floats pinned to the screen)
from.options: Default (with look: fixed, the shape between Sections)
